description: Amends the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 by establishing new mechanisms for regulating social media platforms, removing or blocking unlawful or offensive online content, handling complaints, penalizing false or fake information, and creating the Social Media Protection and Regulatory Authority, Social Media Complaint Council, Social Media Protection Tribunal, and National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency.

source: Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016
description: Provides a legal framework in Pakistan for preventing, investigating, prosecuting, and trying electronic crimes. The Act defines cyber offences such as unauthorized access to information systems or data, data copying or transmission, cyber terrorism, electronic forgery and fraud, identity information misuse, cyber stalking, spamming, spoofing, and unlawful online content. It also establishes procedures for investigation, search and seizure, data preservation, service provider responsibilities, international cooperation, prosecution, trial, appeals, compensation, and preventive measures against electronic crimes.

source: The Balochistan Protection Against Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2016
description: Provides legal protection against harassment of women at the workplace in Balochistan by defining harassment, workplace, employee, employer, complainant, and organization. The Act requires each organization to establish an Inquiry Committee, follow a formal complaint and inquiry procedure, impose minor or major penalties where harassment is proved, and provide appeal mechanisms through an Ombudsperson. It also sets employer responsibilities, requires display and implementation of a workplace Code of Conduct, establishes a helpline for victims, and provides guidance for confidential reporting, investigation, protection from retaliation, and maintaining a harassment-free work environment.

source: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace (Amendment) Act, 2018
description: Amends the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 as applicable in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by substituting Ombudsman with Ombudsperson, limiting the Acts extent to the Province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, updating references to provincial laws and government bodies, revising the definition of organization, setting qualifications and appointment procedures for the Ombudsperson, and providing for representation to the Governor against decisions of the Ombudsperson.

source: The Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 (as applicable in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa)
description: Provides legal protection against harassment of women at the workplace in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by defining harassment, workplace, employee, employer, complainant, organization, Inquiry Committee, and Ombudsperson. The Act requires organizations to form an Inquiry Committee, adopt and display a Code of Conduct, conduct confidential inquiries into harassment complaints, impose minor or major penalties, provide appeal mechanisms through the Ombudsperson, and protect complainants and witnesses from retaliation. It also sets out the powers, appointment, acting role, oath, and complaint-handling functions of the Ombudsperson.

source: The Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace (Amendment) Act, 2021
description: Amends the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 as applicable in Punjab by adding provisions related to the Ombudspersons tenure and resignation. The amendment provides that the Ombudsperson shall hold office for four years, shall not be eligible for extension or re-appointment, and may resign by writing to the Governor.

source: The Punjab Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace (Amendment) Act, 2012
description: Amends the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 as applicable in Punjab by substituting Ombudsman with Ombudsperson, extending the Act to the whole of Punjab, updating references to the Punjab Industrial Relations Act, 2010 and Government of the Punjab, revising the appointment and qualifications of the Ombudsperson, providing representation to the Governor against Ombudsperson decisions, and allowing employer non-compliance complaints to be filed before the Ombudsperson.

source: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace (Amendment) Act, 2022
description: Amends the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 by broadening the definitions of complainant, employee, employer, harassment, Ombudsperson, organization, and workplace. The amendment expands coverage to include former employees, minors through parents or guardians, students, performers, artists, interns, domestic workers, home-based workers, freelance and gig workers, online businesses, and places where services are rendered or performed. It also includes stalking, cyberstalking, gender-based discrimination, child-sensitive procedures, audio and video evidence, professional licence suspension or cancellation, time limits for Ombudsperson decisions, and retaliation through counter-blast defamation suits.

source: Federal Ombudsperson Secretariat for Protection Against Harassment (FOSPAH) â Amina Hassan vs Sharjeel Shahid & others (Final Order)
description: Final order issued by the Federal Ombudsperson under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010, addressing gender-based discrimination at Khushhali Microfinance Bank Limited. The case involves forced resignation, denial of severance benefits compared to male employees, retaliation after complaint, absence of an Inquiry Committee, and employer liability for failing to ensure a harassment-free workplace.

source: Arooj Malik vs Dr Hafiz Ishaq (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of sexual harassment in a university workplace. The case defines harassment through unwelcome physical conduct and sexually explicit communication, examines evidentiary value of text messages and admissions, and establishes that repeated unwanted advances constitute harassment under the Act. It also clarifies jurisdiction of the Ombudsperson where inquiry committees fail to provide fair proceedings and outlines penalties including dismissal from service and monetary compensation for mental agony and suffering.

source: Federal Ombudsperson Secretariat for Protection Against Harassment (FOSPAH) â Asmara Masood vs Syed Arif Hussain (Final Order, 2025)
description: Final order issued by the Federal Ombudsperson under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010, concerning allegations of workplace harassment at Standard Chartered Bank. The case involves claims of sexually inappropriate conduct, hostile work environment, retaliation after complaint, and unlawful termination. The Ombudsperson examined the inquiry proceedings, evidence, and conduct of both parties, and held that the allegations of harassment were not substantiated due to lack of corroborative evidence. The appeal was dismissed, while emphasizing due process, employer inquiry procedures, and the distinction between interpersonal conflict and legally defined workplace harassment.

source: Bahadur Ali Mahar vs Secretary Information and Broadcasting (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning an appeal against a penalty imposed by an Anti-Harassment Committee in a public sector organization. The case examines procedural requirements of inquiry proceedings, including formation of the committee, recording of evidence, and the right of cross-examination, and emphasizes that denial of due process and fair trial renders disciplinary actions invalid. It establishes that inquiry committees must strictly comply with statutory procedures, uphold principles of natural justice, and ensure that both parties are given a fair opportunity to present and challenge evidence before imposing penalties.

source: The Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary and others vs Azhar Ali and others (Civil Appeals No.106-K to 111-K & C.P.L.A. No.650-K of 2024, Supreme Court of Pakistan)
description: Decides civil appeals and petition concerning appointments under the deceased quota policy governed by Rule 11-A of the Sindh Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1974. The case examines whether the High Court could grant employment beyond the prescribed two-year limitation period and considers the impact of subsequent Supreme Court judgment declaring the rule unconstitutional. The Court applies principles of beneficial interpretation of service laws, holds that rights accrued under earlier judgments remain protected due to prospective application of law, and affirms that past and closed transactions cannot be reopened. The appeals are dismissed, upholding High Court orders granting employment benefits under the deceased quota policy.

source: Ayaz Ali vs Federation of Pakistan (Supreme Court, 2025)
description: Provides a judgment concerning employment under the deceased quota policy in a public sector bank. The case examines whether applications submitted under an earlier policy can be denied based on subsequent Supreme Court rulings declaring such quota unconstitutional, and clarifies the doctrine of prospective application of judicial decisions. It establishes that rights accrued under policies in force at the time of application must be considered fairly and cannot be retrospectively invalidated, and emphasizes equal opportunity, non-discriminatory implementation of employment policies, and the obligation of authorities to decide pending applications in accordance with applicable rules.

source: Muhammad Azam and others vs Province of Sindh through Secretary Home Department and others (C.P.L.A. Nos.954-K, 955-K, 966-K, 1034-K to 1040-K of 2025, Supreme Court of Pakistan)
description: Decides civil petitions for leave to appeal concerning withdrawal of promotions of police constables under the Police Rules, 1934 and the legality of alleged out-of-turn or shoulder promotions. The case examines whether promotions granted on merit under Rule 13.6(2) could be retrospectively invalidated following Supreme Court judgments prohibiting out-of-turn promotions. The Court considers principles of fair trial, vested rights, and non-retrospective application of law, and emphasizes the duty of the Service Tribunal to independently assess facts, service record, and applicable rules rather than relying solely on departmental assertions. The impugned judgment is set aside and the matter is remanded for fresh decision in accordance with law after proper evaluation of evidence and opportunity of hearing.

source: Nadia Naz vs President of Pakistan (Supreme Court, 2023)
description: Provides a judgment in review jurisdiction interpreting the definition of harassment under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010. The case clarifies that harassment is not limited to conduct of a sexual nature but also includes gender-based discrimination arising from power dynamics and hostile work environment. It applies purposive interpretation of statutory provisions, considers constitutional principles of dignity and equality, and incorporates international conventions to establish that harassment includes discriminatory behavior based on gender. The Court sets aside earlier judgments for adopting a restrictive interpretation and remands the matter for reconsideration in light of the expanded scope of harassment.

source: Dr. Asma Kiyani vs Dr. Mazhar Hussain (Federal Ombudsperson Secretariat for Protection Against Harassment, Complaint No. FOH-HQR-H/033/2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment, gender-based discrimination, and hostile work environment at the National Institute of Rehabilitation Medicine. The case examines misuse of administrative authority, stalking, retaliation after complaint, unlawful KPI deductions, and initiation of disciplinary proceedings without due process. The Ombudsperson finds that the conduct of the accused constitutes harassment under gender-based discrimination, establishes retaliation and abuse of authority, and imposes a monetary penalty while recommending administrative action to ensure a safe and non-discriminatory workplace environment.

source: Sana Humayoun vs Bilal Khan (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment. The case examines unwelcome conduct, misuse of authority, and retaliatory behavior following complaint, and evaluates evidence including witness statements and documentary material under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies the obligation of employers to ensure a safe working environment, establish inquiry mechanisms, and enforce a code of conduct, and determines liability based on failure to maintain a harassment-free workplace.

source: Faisal Saeed Syed vs Saif Ullah (FOSPAH)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of sexual harassment in a home-based educational setting. The case defines harassment in the context of teacher-student relationships, examines misuse of authority and inappropriate conduct, and clarifies that informal work arrangements and minors fall within the scope of the Act. It also outlines institutional responsibilities to establish inquiry mechanisms, adopt a code of conduct, and ensure a harassment-free environment.

source: Sehar Zareen vs Taeem Ul Haq (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment in a professional setting. The case examines unwelcome conduct, inappropriate behavior, and misuse of authority, and evaluates evidence on the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies the scope of harassment beyond physical acts to include verbal and psychological conduct, and emphasizes the duty of employers to maintain a harassment-free workplace through proper inquiry mechanisms, enforcement of a code of conduct, and protection against retaliation.

source: Zainab Zahrah Awan vs Embrace IT (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment in a private IT organization. The case examines unwelcome conduct, abuse of authority, and retaliatory actions following complaint, and evaluates evidence including digital communication and workplace behavior patterns. It clarifies the scope of employer responsibility to ensure a safe working environment, enforce a code of conduct, and establish effective inquiry mechanisms, and determines liability based on balance of probabilities under the Act.

source: Muhammad Rahman vs Imtiaz Gadar (FOSPAH, 2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of sexual harassment and hostile work environment in a corporate setting. The case examines whether inquiry proceedings were conducted in accordance with statutory requirements, including proper constitution of the inquiry committee and provision of fair trial rights. It clarifies that harassment includes patterns of unwelcome conduct creating a hostile environment and that proceedings initiated under the Act must strictly comply with procedural mandates. The order holds that failure to constitute a valid inquiry committee renders the proceedings void, sets aside the dismissal, and remands the matter for fresh inquiry in accordance with law.

source: Muqaddas Fatima vs Mubashir Mukhtar (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment arising from gender-based discrimination during a sporting event. The case examines misbehavior, physical intimidation, and abuse of authority in a professional setting, and clarifies that harassment is not limited to sexual conduct but includes actions driven by gender-based power dynamics that create a hostile work environment. It applies the principle established in Nadia Naz case that discriminatory and demeaning conduct affecting work performance constitutes harassment, and imposes penalties including stoppage of increments and monetary compensation for the victim.

source: Najma Bahar vs Ibrar Hussain (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment. The case examines unwelcome conduct, misuse of authority, and retaliatory behavior following complaint, and evaluates evidence on the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that harassment includes conduct creating intimidation or humiliation in the workplace and emphasizes the obligation of employers to establish inquiry mechanisms, enforce a code of conduct, and ensure a safe and harassment-free working environment.

source: Najma Bahar vs Ibrar Hussain (FOSPAH, 2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment arising from verbal abuse, physical contact, and creation of a hostile work environment. The case examines evidentiary standards based on affidavits and witness testimony, and establishes that even a single substantiated incident involving abusive language and physical misconduct can constitute harassment under the Act. It clarifies that harassment includes gender-based discrimination and prejudicial conduct creating intimidation and humiliation, and emphasizes that such behavior reflects power imbalance rather than sexual intent. The order finds the accused guilty and imposes a minor penalty of withholding one annual increment for a specified period.

source: Shoaib Zafar vs Tanzeela Soomro (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment in a professional setting. The case examines unwelcome conduct, inappropriate communication, and misuse of authority, and evaluates evidence including digital correspondence and witness statements under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that repeated unwelcome behavior and psychological pressure can constitute harassment even in absence of physical contact, and emphasizes the responsibility of employers to ensure effective inquiry mechanisms, enforce a code of conduct, and maintain a safe and respectful workplace environment.

source: Robina Khalid vs Munir H Shah (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment in a public sector organization. The case examines unwelcome conduct, verbal abuse, and misuse of authority, and evaluates evidence based on witness statements and documentary material under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that persistent intimidating behavior and discriminatory treatment constitute harassment under the Act, and emphasizes the obligation of employers to ensure a safe working environment, establish inquiry mechanisms, and enforce a code of conduct to prevent harassment.

source: Naheed Saghir vs Saud ur Rehman (FOSPAH, 2024)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment. The case examines unwelcome conduct, inappropriate behavior, and misuse of authority, and evaluates evidence including witness statements and documentary material under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that harassment includes conduct creating intimidation, humiliation, or psychological pressure in the workplace, and emphasizes the obligation of employers to establish inquiry mechanisms, enforce a code of conduct, and ensure a safe and harassment-free working environment.

source: Samreen Shahid vs Jamal Baig (FOSPAH, 2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of sexual harassment and hostile work environment in a public sector organization. The case examines unwelcome physical contact, sexually suggestive remarks, coercive behavior, and retaliation through threats of transfer and misuse of authority, and evaluates evidence based on witness testimony and consistency of statements under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that repeated unwelcome conduct and abuse of authority creating an intimidating and offensive work environment constitutes harassment under the Act, and emphasizes that lack of direct eyewitnesses does not negate credible testimony. The order finds the accused guilty, imposes the penalty of removal from service, and highlights the obligation of institutions to ensure safe workplaces, establish effective inquiry mechanisms, and prevent harassment.

source: Sana Humayun vs Bilal Khan (FOSPAH, 2026)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of gender-based discrimination, coercive conduct, and creation of a hostile environment affecting a working womanâs access to residential accommodation. The case examines whether discriminatory housing practices, including denial of residence to single women and disconnection of basic utilities, fall within the scope of harassment where such conduct interferes with professional life. It clarifies that the definition of workplace extends to situations linked to employment and that misuse of organizational authority impacting a womanâs ability to work may constitute harassment. It further establishes that policies denying accommodation on the basis of gender or marital status are discriminatory, void, and inconsistent with principles of equality and dignity, and directs authorities to ensure non-discriminatory access to safe housing for working women.

source: Saneem Afshain vs Azhar Abbas (FOSPAH, 2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment. The case examines unwelcome conduct, inappropriate communication, and misuse of authority, and evaluates evidence including witness statements and documentary material under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that repeated unwelcome behavior and creation of psychological pressure constitute harassment under the Act, and emphasizes the obligation of employers to establish inquiry mechanisms, enforce a code of conduct, and ensure a safe and harassment-free working environment.

source: Dr Asma Kiyani vs Mazhar Hussain (FOSPAH, 2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment arising from abuse of authority, gender-based discrimination, and creation of a hostile work environment in a public health institution. The case examines retaliatory actions, misuse of administrative powers, and initiation of disciplinary proceedings to victimise the complainant, and evaluates evidence under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that harassment includes discriminatory and coercive conduct linked to power imbalance, and emphasizes that retaliation following complaint constitutes a violation of the Act. The order finds the accused responsible, imposes monetary penalty, and directs the organization to ensure compliance with statutory requirements including fair inquiry mechanisms and maintenance of a harassment-free workplace.

source: Faheem Mehmood vs Air University (FOSPAH, 2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and gender-based discrimination in an educational institution. The case examines misuse of authority, hostile work environment, and retaliatory actions affecting employment conditions, and evaluates evidence under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that discriminatory treatment linked to power imbalance and interference with professional duties constitutes harassment under the Act, and emphasizes the responsibility of institutions to establish inquiry mechanisms, enforce a code of conduct, and ensure a safe and harassment-free workplace.

source: Ghulam Haider Butt vs Collectorate of Customs Appraisement Quetta (FOSPAH, 2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and gender-based discrimination in a public sector organization. The case examines misuse of authority, hostile work environment, and retaliatory actions affecting employment conditions, and evaluates evidence under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that discriminatory conduct and abuse of official position that undermines dignity and professional performance constitutes harassment under the Act, and emphasizes the obligation of organizations to ensure fair inquiry procedures, enforce a code of conduct, and maintain a safe and respectful workplace environment.

source: Shergel Shahzad vs Farhan Raheem (FOSPAH, 2025)
description: Provides a final order under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 concerning allegations of workplace harassment and hostile work environment in a professional setting. The case examines unwelcome conduct, inappropriate communication, and misuse of authority, and evaluates evidence including witness statements and documentary material under the standard of balance of probabilities. It clarifies that persistent unwelcome behavior and coercive conduct affecting dignity and professional performance constitute harassment under the Act, and emphasizes the obligation of employers to establish inquiry mechanisms, enforce a code of conduct, and ensure a safe and harassment-free workplace.

description: Federal Ombudsperson decision under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 examining whether derogatory workplace remarks constituted harassment, reviewing inquiry committee due process and cross-examination rights, and setting aside a censure penalty after finding the conduct did not meet the legal threshold for gender-based harassment.

source: Complaint No. FOSPAH/ISB/0004222/2023 â Syed Basit Ali v. State Bank of Pakistan & Others (Federal Ombudsperson)
description: Federal Ombudsperson proceedings under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 involving allegations of workplace harassment, discriminatory conduct, misuse of authority, and retaliatory actions within the State Bank of Pakistan, including claims relating to adverse employment treatment, hostile work environment, and procedural irregularities.

source: Complaint No. FOH-HQR/00297/2024 â Zainab Zahrah Awan v. Embrace IT (Federal Ombudsperson)
description: Federal Ombudsperson decision under the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 holding that termination of a female employee during approved maternity leave constituted gender-based discrimination and unlawful workplace harassment. The order discusses constitutional protections, maternity rights, international human rights obligations, compensation, reinstatement-related relief, and employer obligations regarding safe motherhood and non-discriminatory workplace practices.
